sections.title: The letter C
paragraphs: The letter (C) /k/ makes its main sound in (cat) /kæt/, a small furry pet. A consonant is a sound made when the mouth blocks or narrows the air. This letter has three sounds.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: First, lift the back of your tongue to touch the roof of your mouth. Stop the air, then let it burst out with no voice. Next, put the tip of your tongue near the ridge behind your upper teeth. Push air through the narrow gap to make a hiss. Feel your throat. It does not shake for either sound.

sections.title: Reading this letter
paragraphs: Before the vowels a, o, u or consonants, say the sound in (cup) /kʌp/. Before the vowels e, i or y, say the sound in (city) /sɪ.ti/. Sometimes it is a silent letter, as in (muscle) /mʌs.əl/. A silent letter is a letter that you write but do not say.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not turn the sound into a voiced sound by letting your throat shake. A voiced sound is a sound where the voice is on. Keep your vocal cords relaxed so that you do not say a g instead. When reading words like (indict) /ɪn.daɪt/, do not say the letter out loud.
